data.description:
Source: board DM msg 226 (2026-08-30 21:31, human:forrest -> cto-owen): 'also we should surface loop status on the chat UI here. whether it's active, one tick, or off.'

Goal: the chat app UI (apps/chat) shows, at a glance, which of three states the company loop is in:
1. Loop active — a /loop /advance session is running (continuous ticks).
2. Single tick in flight — one /advance tick is currently executing.
3. Off/idle — nothing running.

Known signal sources (starting points, not a design):
- apps/chat/data/advance.lock — present while a tick is in flight; contains pid/source/startedAt/nonce. The 'source' field may distinguish loop-driven vs watcher/one-off ticks.
- Watcher process state under apps/chat/watch/ (advance-watcher.mjs) — whether the watcher is alive affects what 'off' means.
- Consider staleness: a lock left behind by a dead pid should not read as 'active' (check pid liveness or startedAt age).

Design specifics (polling vs push, where the indicator lives in the UI, how loop-vs-tick is distinguished) are left to the planning stage. Task created on behalf of the board from the DM channel.
data.title: Chat: surface advance-loop status in the UI — active loop / single tick in flight / idle

data.body: Board directive (DM msg 230, human:forrest): implementation kickoff is now implicit for internal-tools work — no per-task board green-light needed. Marcus implements. Normal lifecycle still applies (plan -> implement -> QA review); what's removed is the per-task board wait, not the gates. Sequenced after AS-26 (permalinks first, loop-status builds on it).

CTO ordering call (board DM msg 323). Rank 5 — first of the cosmetic/UX internal-tools items, ranked above AS-32/28/33 because it is the only one with operational value rather than polish value: it answers 'is the company running right now, or waiting on me', which is exactly the question the board is asking when he asks whether anything is blocked. Signal sources unchanged from the description (advance.lock contents plus watcher process state, with staleness handling). Conditional promotion: if the board adopts an unattended heartbeat tick, this jumps to rank 2 — an autonomous loop with no visible run state is a bad trade.
Board directive (DM msg 394): all chat issues ship. Cluster order 2/6 — loop-status surfacing is the highest-leverage board-facing item (tells Forrest whether a tick is running without asking).

Planned 2026-09-03 (cto-owen, on board DM msg 519). Design in the plan file; the load-bearing decisions: (1) ONE staleness predicate — the server imports the watcher's own isLockStale + DEFAULTS.lockStaleMin; the container cannot see host pids (separate pid namespace), so staleness is age-only in-container, and we say so rather than inventing a second rule. (2) Four states, not three: 'off' splits into idle-with-watcher-listening vs off-no-watcher, because that difference decides whether the board's next message fires anything. It needs a watcher heartbeat (advance-watcher.pid gains heartbeatAt, rewritten each 5s poll). (3) Server polls the two files every 2s (fs.watch is untrusted across the bind mount, same reason the watcher polls) and pushes 'loop' SSE frames only on state change; GET /api/loop-status for initial render. (4) The lock nonce is never served. (5) Known limit: a /loop session holds no lock between ticks, so 'loop' shows only while a loop tick runs; lastTick text mitigates. Reassigned to developer-lena: self-contained medium (her lane per record 11 §9 lane doctrine), she is not in flight, and Marcus stays on the D1 spine (AS-70 / AS-45 rework). Handoff note for QA: the running watcher predates the heartbeat and must be restarted by a host session for the indicator to leave 'Off' — a tick cannot do that.

Starting implementation in .worktrees/AS-27 on feat/AS-27-loop-status, per the plan: one staleness predicate imported from the watcher rather than reimplemented, the four states, the nonce never leaving the server, and the between-loop-ticks gap documented as a limit rather than papered over. Note the live constraint: the running watcher (pid 96123) is on pre-AS-27 code and will keep running it until someone restarts it, so the heartbeat field will be absent in production at first — the plan already handles that honestly as listening:false with reason no-heartbeat, which self-corrects on restart.

IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE (developer-lena) — branch feat/AS-27-loop-status, 3 commits, worktree clean, nothing pushed.

FILES TOUCHED (14 files, +1228/-18 vs master; measured `git diff --stat master...HEAD`)
new:  lib/loop-status.js (134), public/loop-status.js (114), test/loop-status.test.js (156), test/loop-label.test.js (133)
mod:  server.js (+129/-1), public/app.js (+46), public/index.html (+6), public/style.css (+18),
      watch/advance-watcher.mjs (+43/-1), test/api.test.js (+190/-8), test/stream.test.js (+151/-4),
      test/watcher.test.js (+42/-1), README.md (+66), watch/README.md (+18/-1)
No compose change (C2 verified: deploy-shape.test.js already pins ./data:/app/data rw — assertion existed, none added).
No .lattice on the branch (`git diff --name-only master...HEAD | grep -c '^.lattice'` = 0).

SUITE — cardinality before quantification.
  before (in-container, master; master == branch base for apps/chat, `git diff 007347c master -- apps/chat` empty):
        235 tests examined, 235 pass, 0 fail
  after (in-container, `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 COMPOSE_DOCKER_CLI_BUILD=1 docker compose run --rm --build test`):
        255 tests examined, 255 pass, 0 fail  (+20)
  host `node --test` agrees at 255/255.

THE FOUR STATES, each with the input that produces it (run end-to-end through deriveLoopStatus + describeLoopStatus):
  loop  <- advance.lock {source:"loop",  startedAt: now-60s}  + pid file with fresh heartbeatAt  -> "Loop active"
  tick  <- advance.lock {source:"watcher", startedAt: now-5s} + pid file with fresh heartbeatAt  -> "Tick in flight · watcher"
          (source "manual" -> "Tick in flight · manual"; the source is never inferred)
  idle  <- no advance.lock                                    + pid file with fresh heartbeatAt  -> "Idle · watcher listening"
  off   <- no advance.lock                                    + no pid file                      -> "Off · no watcher"
4 distinct tones and 4 distinct labels asserted as a set (new Set(...).size === 4) in test/loop-label.test.js, and
4 distinct states asserted as a set through real HTTP in api.test.js — the vacuity shape of this task (one rendering
for every state) cannot pass.

LIVE PRODUCTION READING right now, taken read-only against apps/chat/data (no container touched, nothing written):
  advance.lock    {"pid":5285,"startedAt":"2026-09-03T16:34:15.854Z","source":"loop"}
  advance-watcher.pid {"pid":96123,"startedAt":"2026-08-31T00:39:41.401Z"}   <- no heartbeatAt
  -> state "loop", label "Loop active",
     detail "Loop tick from loop (pid 5285) started 23 min ago. Watcher: the watcher pid file carries no heartbeat,
             so this watcher is running pre-AS-27 code — restart it (launchctl bootout, then bootstrap; ...)"
  nonce present in payload: false.
  This is R3 behaving as planned: watcher 96123 IS alive (confirmed with ps) but nothing in its file says so, so the
  indicator does not claim it. No special-casing was added to make that look better.

MUTATION TESTING — one indivisible step, three mutations, scratch copies OUTSIDE the worktree
(/private/tmp/.../agent-developer-lena/, harness mutate.py). Harness aborts before running if any fixed-string count
mismatches; assert-applied is SCOPED to the edited region and compares the region's COMPLETE line contents against an
expected list (the AS-54 lesson — a presence check passes with a wrong extra line present). Scratch baseline verified
green first (255/255) so the mutant deltas mean something.

  m1 AC-1  lib/loop-status.js: swap the `source === 'loop'` branch ('loop'<->'tick')
     applied: 5-line region matched exactly. predicted 6 failing; observed 6, same set:
       - AS-27 loop-status: the four states, each from the inputs that produce it
       - AS-27 loop-status: staleness boundary is the watcher's, not a second comparison
       - AS-27 loop-status: a startedAt in the future (host clock skew) reads as age 0, never negative
       - api: AS-27 - GET /api/loop-status reports each of the four states from its own file configuration
       - api: AS-27 - the AS-16 nonce never leaves the server, and malformed files never 500
       - stream: AS-27 - a new lock pushes exactly one loop frame; an unchanged lock pushes none over ten polls
     The idle/off, malformed-input, nonce-key and label tests correctly did NOT move — the plan's "the loop and tick
     cases fail, nothing else" holds.

  m2 AC-5  server.js: neuter the changed-check (`if (key === lastLoopKey) return;` -> `{ /* emit anyway */ }`)
     applied: 5-line region matched exactly. predicted 1-3 failing; observed exactly 1:
       - stream: AS-27 - a new lock pushes exactly one loop frame; an unchanged lock pushes none over ten polls
     Narrower than my worst case, and I checked why rather than accepting it: the other two AS-27 stream tests survive
     because their assertions land before enough spurious frames buffer. Under the REAL code they are deterministic
     (zero frames are emitted at all until a state-bearing field changes), so this is a property of the mutant, not a
     weak test. The zero-frame count is the guard that matters and it died.

  m3 AC-9  watch/advance-watcher.mjs: drop `heartbeatAt` from the pid-file body
     applied: 4-line region matched exactly. predicted 1 failing; observed exactly 1:
       - writeWatcherPid: atomic {pid, startedAt, heartbeatAt}; heartbeats advance without losing startedAt

  Restoration proved by content-hash manifest over apps/chat (72 files, sha256 each): identical before and after,
  and `git status --porcelain` in the worktree is empty. The worktree was never mutated, so no rebuild was needed
  (the image built for the 255/255 in-container run is still the tree that is committed).

WATCHER CHANGE AND ITS BLAST RADIUS (the watcher is the thing that fires ticks, so stating this plainly):
  - Added exported writeWatcherPid({path,pid,startedAt,now}): tmp + renameSync, body {pid, startedAt, heartbeatAt}.
  - main() calls it once at startup (unguarded — no marker means no single-instance guard, fail loud) and at the TOP
    of poll(), BEFORE the `if (child) return` early path, wrapped in try/catch.
  - Why guarded there (deviation 1 below): poll() runs inside setInterval. An unguarded throw (full disk, permissions)
    becomes an uncaught exception that kills the watcher — and then NO message ever fires a tick again, silently.
    A swallowed heartbeat costs a wrong indicator for 60s. That asymmetry decided it.
  - If I got this wrong: the failure mode is the write itself, not the decision logic — decide()/isLockStale/fire()
    are untouched, so fire/skip behaviour is bit-identical to before. The realistic bad outcome is pid-file churn
    (one small atomic write per 5s poll) or, if renameSync failed persistently, a stray advance-watcher.pid.tmp; the
    single-instance check reads `pid` from the real path only and would be unaffected. Worst case the indicator lies;
    the loop does not stop.
  - R1 discharged: `grep -rn 'advance-watcher\.pid' apps/ .claude/` finds 3 hits — the watcher's own paths entry and
    two watch/README.md mentions. No other reader exists to break on the added key.
  - THE RUNNING WATCHER (pid 96123) IS ON PRE-AS-27 CODE and will stay there until someone restarts it. Until then
    the indicator says "Off · no watcher" whenever no tick holds the lock. That restart is a HOST action for the board
    or a live session (launchctl bootout then bootstrap) — a headless tick has no launchctl reach. Documented in
    watch/README.md under a new "After any change to this watcher: restart it" heading.

LITERALS THAT MOVED, and confirmation the not-moving set did not:
  moved/new: WATCHER_STALE_MS = 60_000 (new, lib/loop-status.js; = 12 x DEFAULTS.pollS, asserted arithmetically so it
             cannot drift from the watcher's cadence silently); LOOP_POLL_MS = 2_000 (new, exported from server.js);
             two new CSS hexes #2eb67d (loop) and #ecb22e (tick) — see deviation 3; a 15_000 local render interval in
             app.js — see deviation 2.
  NOT moved, confirmed: DEFAULTS.lockStaleMin (45) — imported, never restated, and the existing `config: defaults
             match the plan` test still pins all of it; DEFAULTS.pollS (5); HEARTBEAT_MS (25_000); the 60_000
             reconcile poll in app.js; every existing STATIC_FILES entry (one added, none changed); the compose
             mounts and the Dockerfile.

DEVIATIONS (numbered; each the smallest thing that satisfies the intent)
  1. Plan §4.4 does not say the poll-time heartbeat is guarded. I wrapped it in try/catch. Rationale above: an
     unguarded throw inside setInterval kills the watcher, which is a strictly worse failure than a stale indicator.
     Startup write left unguarded, deliberately.
  2. Plan §4.2 fixes LOOP_POLL_MS at 2s with no knob. I exported the constant and added an optional `loopPollMs`
     option to createChatServer (default = the exported constant). AC-5 requires counting frames over ten real poll
     cycles; at 2s that is a 20-second sleep in the suite. The tests inject 25ms so ten cycles are ten cycles. The
     property under test is the frame COUNT, which the cadence does not affect, and api.test.js pins both
     LOOP_POLL_MS === 2_000 and that the default is the exported constant, so the shipping cadence cannot drift.
  3. Plan §4.3 says "keep to the existing colour vocabulary; no new tokens." The file has no light green and no amber
     that reads against the #3f0e40 sidebar (its greens #007a5a/#148567 disappear into it). I added exactly two hexes,
     #2eb67d and #ecb22e, both in the same Slack-derived family as the existing #3f0e40/#1164a3/#e01e5a; idle and off
     reuse the sidebar's own #bfa8c0 and #5b2c5c. No CSS custom properties were introduced.
  4. Two shared TEST-HELPER changes a reviewer should look at closely, both consequences of AC-6 rather than
     conveniences:
     (a) stream.test.js openStream() now consumes the on-connect `loop` frame into `initialLoop` (and throws if the
         first frame is not one). This keeps nextFrame() meaning "the next MESSAGE frame", so the AS-25 hidden-channel
         ordering proof and the pending()===0 assertions are untouched, and it makes the on-connect contract asserted
         by every stream test rather than one.
     (b) Both stream.test.js and api.test.js bootServer now default dataDir to a scratch path. Without it the suite
         would read the REAL apps/chat/data and a live tick could flip a test's expected state mid-run. This extends
         the file's existing mountless invariant to the two new files.
  5. The AS-25 interval guard in api.test.js was WIDENED, not loosened, and this is the one place I changed an
     existing assertion. Old: "exactly one setInterval, and it is >= 30s". A 15s render-only timer would have failed
     it on a count. New: exactly two intervals; exactly one of them issues requests; that one is >= 30s; the other
     matches no /refreshSidebar|api\(|fetch\(/ at all. That states the property AS-25 actually cared about (nothing
     refetches on a short cadence) instead of counting timers. If the reviewer disagrees, this is the line to argue.
  6. Reason strings are slightly richer than the plan's shape: staleLock carries 'bad-startedAt' (and 'unparsable')
     alongside isLockStale's own 'age'. The finite-startedAt check is ordered before isLockStale purely so the reason
     names the real defect; it can never turn a stale lock fresh, and isLockStale remains the sole freshness authority.

LEFT UNDONE
  - AC-12 (manual verification against the running app) is NOT done and I could not do it. It needs (a) the container
    rebuilt on this branch and (b) the host watcher restarted; both are outside a task worktree's reach, the deploy
    half is the subject of AS-75, and my instructions forbid touching asc-chat-server-1 (8347), which was just
    deployed and is serving the board. What I did instead is the read-only production reading quoted above, which
    exercises the real files through the real derivation. AC-12 should be executed by the board or a live session
    after merge + rebuild + watcher restart.
  - Out of scope per plan §4.6 and untouched: the `chat loop-status` CLI, and any change making a loop announce
    itself between ticks (that is an advance.md change, i.e. metawork).

WHERE THE REVIEWER SHOULD START
  1. lib/loop-status.js header + the isLockStale call site — the one-predicate rule and the pidAlive:true comment.
  2. The two test-helper changes and the widened AS-25 guard (deviations 4 and 5): those touch shared machinery.
  3. server.js loopStateKey() — the deliberate exclusion of every age field from the emission comparison, which is
     what makes AC-5's zero-frame count possible.

Orchestrator verification and review assignment.

VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: 14 files, +1228/-18; the live watcher (pid 96123) is still running and unharmed; the nonce appears in the status modules only as a comment explaining why it is excluded, never as a field; and the watcher diff touches only the pid-file writer — decide(), isLockStale() and fire() are untouched, so fire and skip behaviour is bit-identical to what is running now.

THE WATCHER CHANGE IS THE RISKIEST THING IN THIS BRANCH AND THE IMPLEMENTER HANDLED IT CORRECTLY. The heartbeat write sits at the top of poll(), which runs inside setInterval — an unguarded throw there would kill the watcher and silently stop every future message-fired tick, which is the mechanism the board's own messages travel on. She wrapped it in try/catch with the trade stated: a swallowed heartbeat costs a wrong indicator for sixty seconds, a thrown one costs the company its ears. That is the right way round, and it is a deviation she recorded rather than a choice she made quietly.

THE PRODUCTION READING IS THE PART I WANT KEPT. She read the real data dir read-only and got: lock pid 5285, source loop, so Loop active; pid file with no heartbeat, so the detail names the watcher restart. The running watcher IS alive — confirmed with ps — and nothing in its file says so, and she did not special-case around that to make the indicator look better than the evidence. An indicator that lied here would be worse than no indicator, because the board would trust it.

FOUR STATES ASSERTED AS A SET rather than individually, so an indicator rendering the same thing everywhere cannot pass. That is the vacuity shape of this task and it is closed by construction.

ONE MUTATION CAME OUT NARROWER THAN PREDICTED and she chased it rather than accepting it — establishing that the two surviving tests survive as a property of the mutant's timing rather than through weak assertions. A narrower observed set is the direction that usually hides a weak test; checking which it was is the whole difference.

AC-12 IS HONESTLY LEFT UNDONE: manual verification against the running app needs the container rebuilt and the watcher restarted, both outside a worktree's reach. The deploy half is AS-75 and the watcher restart is a host action. She substituted the read-only production reading and said so rather than claiming the criterion.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE BOARD, worth stating plainly at merge: the indicator will read "Off - no watcher" until the running watcher is restarted onto the new code, because the heartbeat field it reads does not exist yet. That is correct behaviour and it self-corrects on restart, but it will look like a bug for the minutes between merge and restart, so the restart should follow the merge closely.

REVIEW: assigning agent:qa-priya. Lena implemented, so implementer != reviewer holds; Ruben took AS-32 last. The surface to attack is the one-predicate rule and whether the four states are genuinely distinguishable from the outside rather than only in the pure module.
